title: Compact-support base change at finite coefficients
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type and admit a compactification $c=(j,p)$, with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $g:Y'\to Y$ any morphism. Form the cartesian compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square] with projections $g':X'=X\times_Y Y'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, and the base-changed compactification $c'=(j',p')$. For every complex $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the exchange map of [def-cbc-exchange-map]
$$\operatorname{Ex}_!^c(K):g^{-1}Rf_!^cK\longrightarrow Rf'_!^{c'}g'^{-1}K$$
is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y'_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, where $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. The maps agree under the canonical comparisons obtained from the proper/open refinement maps [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], independently of $c$ and of the common refinement used to compare compactifications [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Consequently they define the compactification-independent map $\operatorname{Ex}_!:g^{-1}Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_!g'^{-1}K$. They are natural in $K$, are identities for identity base changes, and satisfy horizontal and vertical pasting after inserting the canonical inverse-image associativity and compact-support composition isomorphisms. Vertical pasting is asserted for composable compact-support squares (so compactifications of both morphisms and their composite are supplied); composition is computed using the compatible towers of [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. No hypothesis on $g$ or on residue characteristics, no constructibility, and no qcqs hypothesis on the base schemes is required.

proof.text: Use the supplied compactification $c=(j,p)$. [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] gives its base-changed compactification and refinements under arbitrary $g$. The upper open square is cartesian by the fibre-product construction in [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Write $M=j_!K$. Exactness in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] allows degreewise $j_!$ to descend to $D^+$; a representative zero below a fixed degree stays zero there. By [def-cbc-exchange-map], the map to prove invertible is exactly $(Rp'_*\beta_K)\circ\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,p}(M)$, with $\beta:\bar g'^{-1}j_!\cong j'_!g'^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, construction before lemma-shriek-well-defined; blueprint proof first displayed composite

proof.text: The additive group of finite $\Lambda$ has finite exponent: for each $a\in\Lambda$ two nonnegative multiples coincide, so a positive integer kills $a$; multiplying these integers over all elements gives $N>0$ with $N\Lambda=0$. Then $N1_\Lambda=0$, so $Nx=(N1_\Lambda)x=0$ for every element of every $\Lambda$-module. Thus the underlying abelian cohomology sheaves of $M$ are torsion. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the proper $p$, its cartesian square and the bounded-below underlying abelian complex. Its exchange is invertible. The exact forgetful comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] identifies this map with the underlying map of the specific module exchange in step 1 and reflects invertibility. Hence $\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{*,p}(M)$ is invertible. No prime invertibility or constructibility is used.

source.place: Tag 0DDE, label lemma-proper-base-change (bounded-below complexes with torsion cohomology), deduced from Tag 095T, label theorem-proper-base-change; applied to the proper factor as in the blueprint

proof.text: Apply [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] to the upper open square from step 1. It gives precisely the invertible $\beta_K$ in [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Applying $Rp'_*$ preserves its inverse (the image of $\beta_K^{-1}$). Therefore the composite in step 1 has inverse $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}^{-1}\circ Rp'_*(\beta_K^{-1})$, which proves invertibility. Both factors are natural transformations: the proper exchange is the unit/counit composite specified in the definition and $\beta$ is natural by the cited corollary. Their composite is consequently natural in $K$.

source.place: Tag 03S6, label lemma-shriek-base-change (abelian sheaves and module sheaves); blueprint proof first paragraph

proof.text:
For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$ write $p_1=p_2u$ and let $u'$ be its base change. By [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], $\alpha_u:j_{2!}\to Ru_*j_{1!}$ is the refinement comparison; [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] identifies it with $\gamma$ for the square with left vertical identity, right vertical $u$, and opens $j_1,j_2$. Put $C_u=Rp_{2,*}\alpha_u:F_{c_2}\to F_{c_1}$, inserting direct-image composition. The base-change equation for $\gamma$ reads
$$ Ru'_*\beta_1\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,u}(j_{1!})\circ\bar g_2^{-1}\alpha_u
=\alpha_{u'}g'^{-1}\circ\beta_2.$$
Apply $Rp'_{2,*}$ and precede by $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p_2}(j_{2!})$. Naturality moves $\alpha_u$ past this latter exchange. The vertical proper-exchange equation [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], applied directly to the module-coefficient adjunctions in [def-cbc-exchange-map], identifies the two successive proper exchanges for $p_2,u$ with the exchange for $p_1$. This yields the explicit comparison square
$$ C_{u'}g'^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{c_2}=\operatorname{Ex}_!^{c_1}\circ g^{-1}C_u.$$
Thus a refinement comparison intertwines the compact-support exchange maps, rather than merely comparing their objects.

The comparison maps $\alpha_u$ are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso] and obey $\alpha_{vu}=(Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v$, $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-composition]. Use the normalized composition isomorphisms and the identity and triple-composition equations of [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] for ordinary etale $D^+$ with constant-ring modules. These give the associativity normalization of the direct-image composition in $C_u=Rp_{2,*}\alpha_u:F_{c_2}\to F_{c_1}$. Expanding $C_{vu}$, the comparison-composition equation replaces $\alpha_{vu}$ by $(Rv_*\alpha_u)\alpha_v$, and naturality moves the compositor past $\alpha_u$. Associativity identifies the two parenthesizations. Thus $C_{vu}=C_uC_v$ and $C_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; all $C_u$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined; cancellation in the blueprint refinement paragraph

proof.text: For compactifications $c,d$, choose $e\xrightarrow{r}c$, $e\xrightarrow{s}d$ by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] and put $I_{c,d}=C_s^{-1}C_r:F_c\to F_d$. The previous step makes $c\mapsto F_c$ a functor from the cofiltered compactification category to the opposite of the category of functors $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\to D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, sending all arrows to isomorphisms. Apply [lem-cbc-cofiltered-span-comparison] to the ordered pair $(d,c)$, using arrows $s,r$ in that order. Passing its common-predecessor ratio from the opposite category to the original category reverses composition and gives precisely $C_s^{-1}C_r:F_c\to F_d$. Hence $I_{c,d}$ is independent of the common refinement and of its arrows, as an actual natural transformation.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined; cancellation in the blueprint refinement paragraph

proof.text:
Choose a common refinement $e$ of $c,d,k$, using [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] twice. Computing each ratio through $e$ gives $I_{d,k}I_{c,d}=(C_{e\to k}^{-1}C_{e\to d})(C_{e\to d}^{-1}C_{e\to c})=I_{c,k}$; taking the same two arrows gives $I_{c,c}=\mathrm{id}$. Base change preserves the common-refinement data by the same node. Apply step 4 to $r,s$ and cancel $C_{s'}$ to obtain
$$I_{c',d'}g'^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=\operatorname{Ex}_!^d\circ g^{-1}I_{c,d}.$$
This constructs the canonical ordinary etale comparisons and proves independence of the exchange.

source.place: Tag 0F7I, lemma-shriek-well-defined; cancellation in the blueprint refinement paragraph

proof.text: For an identity base change, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] makes the proper factor the identity after inserting the unit isomorphisms; [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] makes $\beta$ the identity too. Their composite is the identity. For two successive base changes $g,h$, compute all compactifications by base-changing $c$. Expand the two composite maps as the four factors $h^{-1}\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}$, $h^{-1}Rp'_*\beta_g$, $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p'}$ and $Rp''_*\beta_h$. Naturality of $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p'}$ moves $\beta_g$ through it. The proper horizontal pasting equation combines the two proper factors, and the open horizontal pasting equation combines $h^{-1}\beta_g$ and $\beta_h$. The result is exactly the two-factor formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map] for $gh$. These equations are proved directly for modules using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], not inferred from faithfulness of derived forgetting: the latter is not assumed. Inverse-image composition is termwise pullback along composite maps; both associativity maps preserve every fibre-product projection, so their square isomorphisms paste. The unit/counit mate formula is explicitly the module formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Apply clauses (1), (2), (4) of the generic mate theorem to these pasted or identity inverse-image squares to obtain respectively the horizontal, vertical and identity proper-exchange equations. The direct-image composition is normalized as in step 5. For each change of compactification, the comparison square of step 7 conjugates both sides by the same invertible comparisons; cancellation proves the equation for those choices.

proof.text:
For vertically pasted squares with $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{h}Z$, use [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] to choose $Y\xrightarrow{i}\bar Y\xrightarrow{q}Z$, $X\xrightarrow{a}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}\bar Y$, and $U=\bar X\times_{\bar Y}Y$, with opens $c:X\to U$, $b:U\to\bar X$, $a=bc$, and proper $p_Y:U\to Y$. These and their base changes compute $F=Rp_{Y,*}c_!$, $H=Rq_*i_!$ and $E=R(qp)_*a_!$. Define the tower composition isomorphism by
$$\mu:HF=Rq_*i_!Rp_{Y,*}c_!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\gamma c_!}Rq_*Rp_*b_!c_!\xrightarrow{\sim}E.$$
Here $\gamma$ is the normalized invertible open/proper comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. The last arrow uses the coherent ordinary etale direct-image compositor of [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] and $b_!c_!\cong a_!$ of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. Exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] gives the degreewise derived version of the latter, with the same unit and associativity equations.

source.place: Tags 0F7J and 0F7F, composition tower and base-change equation; blueprint final sentence

proof.text:
For this fixed tower expand the two compact-support exchanges by [def-cbc-exchange-map]. The base-change equation of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] moves $\gamma:i_!Rp_{Y,*}\to Rp_*b_!$ through pullback: it identifies the factor $i_!Rp_{Y,*}$ with its base-changed counterpart, using its displayed proper exchanges and open comparisons. The successive proper factors for $q,p$ then combine by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], applied to the module adjunctions, with the direct-image normalization of step 5. The open factors for $b,c$ combine by [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change], whose composition clause uses the canonical $b_!c_!\cong a_!$. Naturality moves each adjacent open comparison through the remaining proper exchange. The two surviving factors are $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,qp}(a_!K)$ followed by the extension-by-zero comparison for $a$, precisely the exchange for $hf$. Thus
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{!,hf}\circ g^{-1}\mu=\mu' g_X^{-1}\circ(Rh'_!\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f})\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,h}Rf_!).$$
Here $g$ is the base change on $Z$ and $g_X$ its projection on $X$; all exchange maps are the specified module maps.

source.place: Tags 0F7J and 0F7F, composition tower and base-change equation; blueprint final sentence

proof.text:
For a refinement from tower 1 to tower 2, [lem-cbc-tower-composition-refinement] gives
$$C_{hf}\circ\mu_2=\mu_1\circ(C_hF_1)\circ(H_2C_f).$$
Its hypotheses hold for all proper maps $u,v,w$ and all commuting arrows supplied by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]; it requires no cartesian hypothesis for $vb_1=b_2w$. Any two towers have a common refining tower by that same node. The invertibility and cocycle equations of steps 5–7 allow cancellation of $C_f,C_h,C_{hf}$ in the displayed equation. Hence the composition isomorphism computed in step 9 is independent of the tower after the canonical comparisons. Apply this both before and after base change, and use the comparison square of step 7 to conjugate the equation of step 10. Cancellation gives the stated vertical pasting equation for all supplied compactifications, still on ordinary etale $D^+$ and with no condition on $g$.

lean.statement: theorem compactSupportFiniteTorsion (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {g' : X' ⟶ X} [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (c : Compactification f) : (∀ K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)), IsIso ((rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlusBaseChangeMap Λ sq c).app K)) ∧ (∀ (d : Compactification f) (r : c.Refinement d) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))), compactSupportProperOpenRefinementMap Λ r K = ((derivedPlusFormalism (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).shriekIso d c).hom.app K)
lean.note: Mixed record: the new theorem supplies objectwise invertibility and identifies every specified proper/open refinement map with the canonical shriekIso, without requiring the refinement square to be Cartesian. The recorded existing upstream declarations supply identity, horizontal pasting, compactification-independent exchange, vertical pasting, and composition computed by any compatible tower. They specialize to derivedPlusFormalism (ModuleCat Λ); its HasBaseChange, HasProperExchange and HasProperBaseChange instances require only the finite coefficient ring. QuasiCompact and HasCompactification hypotheses in the canonical clauses follow from finite type, the supplied compactifications and their base changes. The general proper/open comparison is deliberately not replaced by upstream refinementComparison, which has an additional Cartesian-square argument.
